title: Richmond's Streetcars, 1925
subtitle: Sixteen car lines and the places they ran to, in the city that gave the world the electric streetcar
note: Lines follow today's streets, placed from the City Planning Commission's plate of the 1925 routes and the sources cited for each; some ends are approximate. Buildings are today's that stood by 1925, by the city's recorded year built, with lost ones traced from the Sanborn sheets, their outlines and heights approximate.

page.title: Richmond's streetcars, 1925
page.summary: The 1925 car lines and fourteen places they ran to, drawn from a 1943 planning plate and the buildings standing then.
page.intro: By May 1888 Frank Sprague's electric cars were running on Richmond's hills, the first big electric street railway that worked, and the city grew out along the lines. This map draws the system as it stood in 1925: sixteen car lines over the buildings then standing, with fourteen places the cars ran to framed around it, from the suburbs they made to the trolley parks at the ends of the line.
page.image_alt: The 1925 map, framed by its fourteen stops

table.heading: The lines
table.intro: Each line follows the streets its sources name, placed on today's streets. Where a source is silent, the ends are approximate.

page.how: The routes come from plate 53 of Harland Bartholomew & Associates' 1943 report to the City Planning Commission, *Early Transit Routes, 1888 & 1925*, with the details from the sources listed for each line. Buildings are the ones standing today that the city assessor dates to 1925 or before, plus those traced from Sanborn fire-insurance maps downtown; small streets are drawn only where a house of the year stood nearby. Henrico County keeps no such dates online, so the suburbs across the 1925 county line look emptier than they were. On the big map, lines and cars are drawn three times life size; on the single-stop prints, one and a half.
